input_signals.name: AccrualIssuanceRankProduct
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual-inflated earnings are most misleading when the firm is simultaneously tapping external capital markets, because outside funding both enables the balance-sheet build and gives managers incentive to inflate reported earnings before pricing the issue.
input_signals.reasoning: The multiplicative rank form activates the accrual penalty only among net issuers and mutes it for self-funded, cash-generating firms, so the extreme long-short buckets are populated by pure "accrual-financed" cases rather than by high-accrual firms in general. Both channels are scaled by assets and ranked cross-sectionally, keeping the interaction dimensionless and robust to outliers. Higher values should forecast lower returns as accruals reverse and issuance proceeds fail to earn their cost of capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: SoftFundingIntensity
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr))), at), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The fraction of the asset base supported by "soft" funding, meaning non-cash accrual earnings plus net external capital raised, measures how little of the firm's growth is backed by internally generated cash.
input_signals.reasoning: Summing accrual dollars and net external financing dollars before scaling by assets creates a single funding-quality ratio in which the two themes are economically commensurate (both are dollars financing the balance sheet not produced by operations). Unlike a rank composite, it preserves magnitude information, so a firm with extreme accruals and modest issuance is treated similarly to the reverse case, while cash-rich firms retiring capital sit at the bottom. High soft-funding intensity should forecast low abnormal returns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ) ), at ), 1 )

input_signals.name: SustainedAccrualExternalFunding
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), 3), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose earnings have been accrual-heavy on average over three years and that have cumulatively absorbed large external capital over the same window are running a chronically non-self-funding business model, and this sustained state — not a single-year event — is what predicts reversal and underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the 0-5 integer count with a continuous three-year mean accrual ratio and a three-year cumulative financing flow scaled by current assets eliminates the tie-heavy coarse sort while preserving the persistence idea, and a three-year window keeps coverage far higher than five years. The rank product still switches the accrual penalty on only for firms that actually consumed outside capital, so the extreme buckets are large and continuously populated rather than defined by a rare joint event.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithoutPayoutCertification
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(prstkc, 0)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash distributions certify that reported profits are real; therefore the accrual penalty should be concentrated in firms that pay out nothing, and should be largely switched off for firms with high accruals that are nonetheless returning substantial cash to shareholders.
input_signals.reasoning: The additive rank difference has been replaced by a multiplicative form in which the accrual rank is amplified by the rank of negative payout intensity, so the formula now literally implements the stated conditioning: high accruals plus zero payout scores near the maximum, while high accruals plus large dividends and buybacks scores near zero. Using gross distributions rather than net issuance flows makes the certification channel (commitment to pay cash) economically distinct from a net external-financing measure, and COALESCE to zero is the correct convention because a non-reported payout means no payout.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), coalesce( prstkc, 0 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalBloatEquityFunded
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Receivable and inventory build net of operating payables that is paid for with net new equity capital combines the two classic overvaluation symptoms: soft, reversible operating assets on the balance sheet and managers willing to sell shares at current prices to fund them.
input_signals.reasoning: The contaminated share-count growth leg is replaced by net equity issuance in dollars from the cash-flow statement (sstk minus prstkc, scaled by assets), which is immune to splits and stock dividends and measures actual capital raised rather than mechanical share-count changes. The balance-sheet working-capital accrual construction is retained because it captures channel-stuffing and inventory bloat more sharply than aggregate accruals, and the rank product keeps the penalty confined to firms that genuinely financed that bloat externally rather than from operating cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CleanSurplusFundedWCBloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working-capital bloat funded by newly raised outside capital predicts poor returns; measuring that capital from the balance sheet (debt increase plus the clean-surplus residual of equity growth not explained by retained earnings) captures the same economics as cash-flow issuance data but for the full cross-section.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 winner used exactly this mechanism but its financing leg (sstk minus prstkc) restricted coverage to ~10% of firm-months, which caps portfolio t-stats regardless of effect size. Clean surplus gives net external equity as DELTA(ceq) minus (ib minus dividends), and adding the change in total debt yields net capital raised from universally reported balance-sheet items, so a similar per-observation effect should translate into a materially more reliable FF5 alpha. COALESCE(dvc,0) is justified because a non-reported dividend means no dividend was paid.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: IssuerGatedAccrualMagnitude
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1), INDICATOR(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among net external financers the accrual effect should be strong and monotone in the size of the accrual, while among self-funded firms it should be economically negligible; a hard gate plus preserved accrual magnitude therefore extracts more spread than a soft rank product.
input_signals.reasoning: The rank-product family compresses accrual magnitude into a uniform [0,1] score, so extreme accrual firms get no extra weight; this variant keeps winsorized magnitude and switches the signal off entirely for non-financers, sending them to a neutral middle bucket. Comparing it against the gen-0 rank product tells us whether the payoff comes from gating or from magnitude, which is the single most useful design lesson available at this stage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ), indicator( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: SoftAssetStockOnRaisedCapital
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(wcap, che), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 3), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 3), TS_SUM(SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)), 3))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The accumulated stock of non-cash working capital, not just this year's flow, measures how much of the balance sheet consists of soft, reversible assets; when that stock has been built up over several years of net capital infusions rather than retained cash earnings, valuation is most exposed to write-downs.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen-0 tested a flow-accrual times cumulative-flow-financing version (SustainedAccrualExternalFunding) which had the weakest Fama-MacBeth slope of the accepted set, suggesting smoothed flows blur the signal; a stock-versus-multi-year-financing formulation instead contrasts levels, which is the natural way to express balance-sheet bloat. Both legs come from balance-sheet items with three-year clean-surplus accounting for external equity, so coverage should stay well above the cash-flow-based signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( wcap, che ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( dltt, 3 ), sub( delta( ceq, 3 ), ts_sum( sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), 3 ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AbnormalAccrualSpikeAtCapitalRaise
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 4), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings management is a timing phenomenon: what matters is not whether a firm is permanently accrual-intensive (an industry and business-model trait) but whether accruals spike above the firm's own recent norm precisely in the year it raises outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the cross-sectional accrual rank with TS_RANK against the firm's own four-year history converts the accrual leg into a firm-relative abnormality measure, which absorbs permanent industry and business-model differences far more directly than an industry rank while testing a different economic object — opportunistic timing rather than chronic accounting style. Pairing it with the clean-surplus balance-sheet financing leg (debt change plus equity growth unexplained by retained earnings) keeps the financing measure free of the sparse cash-flow-statement fields, so this addresses the coverage bottleneck instead of leaving it untouched.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 4 ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: BookTaxGapFinancedGrowth
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(txp, 0), 1), at))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accruals that are not accompanied by a rise in taxes payable are the ones least likely to reflect real economic income, because managers inflate book income without incurring a cash tax obligation; such earnings become actively misleading when the firm is also raising outside capital against them.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal has used the same undifferentiated accrual measure, so this tests a genuinely new accounting-quality dimension — the book-tax divergence — as the accrual leg while holding the high-coverage clean-surplus financing leg constant. Treating an unreported taxes-payable balance as zero is the economically correct convention, and differencing it means the leg measures the change in tax obligation rather than a level that would merely proxy for profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), ratio( delta( coalesce( txp, 0 ), 1 ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConjunctiveBloatAndCapitalRaise
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The overvaluation state requires both conditions to hold at once — soft working-capital build *and* outside funding — so the signal should be the weaker of the two ranks: a firm cannot qualify by having extreme accruals alone or extreme financing alone.
input_signals.reasoning:
A rank product lets one extreme leg compensate for a mediocre other leg, so the short decile of the archive's best signals is partly populated by pure-accrual or pure-issuance firms; MIN enforces a strict conjunction, which should purify the extreme buckets and lift ls_talpha without any point mass or degenerate ties. This abandons the dividend-yield weighting entirely — answering the concern that the added leg was a known standalone predictor with an opposing sign — and instead tests an operator-structure question (conjunction versus product) using the two legs that have performed best in the archive.
REASONING_NOTE: full support, no zero mass, coverage equal to the clean-surplus family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: PayoutStrainExternallyFunded
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at))), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(dvc, 0), ADD(ABS(ib), COALESCE(dvc, 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A dividend that is large relative to the firm's own earnings power is a commitment the firm cannot fund internally; when that strained commitment coexists with accrual-heavy earnings and fresh outside capital, the distribution is being financed by investors rather than by operations and is vulnerable to a cut.
input_signals.reasoning:
The previous conditioner (dvc/at minus ib/at) was dominated by negative ROA, so unprofitable non-payers loaded highest and the formula measured the profitability effect instead of payout strain; the revised leg dvc/(|ib| + dvc) is bounded in [0,1], equals zero for every non-payer regardless of profitability, and rises only when dividends are large relative to the *magnitude* of earnings. Using |ib| rather than ib also removes the sign inversion for loss-makers, so the leg now measures exactly the strain concept in the hypothesis and no longer double-counts the accrual leg's low-earnings content.
INTERACTION_TYPE_NOTE: conditional
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), add( abs( ib ), coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryFinancingShockOnBloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at), 4))
input_signals.hypothesis: Habitual external financers are correctly priced as such by investors; what is not priced is a firm that turns to the capital markets at an unusual rate *for itself* in the same year its working capital balloons, because that combination reveals a newly emerged funding gap rather than a stable business model.
input_signals.reasoning:
This replaces the size tilt — which was mechanically a size sort and contradicted the evidence that accrual and issuance mispricing concentrates in small firms — with a firm-relative financing shock measured by TS_RANK against the firm's own four-year financing history. It is the untested mirror of AbnormalAccrualSpikeAtCapitalRaise (firm-relative accruals, strong FMB but no alpha), so evaluating it tells us which leg benefits from own-history normalization and which needs a cross-sectional level, at essentially unchanged coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE_FINAL: conditional
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ), ts_rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ), 4 ) )

input_signals.name: DualSidedWorkingCapitalStrain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Netting payables against receivables and inventory, as the standard accrual definition does, cancels two symptoms that are economically reinforcing: a firm that is simultaneously building soft assets, stretching its suppliers, and raising outside capital is drawing on every available funding source at once.
input_signals.reasoning: Standard working-capital accruals treat a payables build as a *credit* that offsets asset bloat, but stretched trade credit is itself a strain indicator, so the netted measure discards information; this decomposes the two sides and requires both to be high alongside external financing. It is a genuine re-specification of the accrual construct rather than a re-weighting, uses only balance-sheet items so coverage stays near the top of the archive, and its failure would be equally informative in confirming that netting is the correct accounting.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityRaisedToPayDividends
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(MIN(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0))), COALESCE(dvc, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Selling equity while simultaneously paying dividends is the most economically indefensible round trip a firm can execute — it is tax-inefficient, dilutive, and rational only if management believes the stock is overpriced — and it is a warning of overvaluation precisely when the earnings backing the dividend are accrual-based rather than cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's MIN-overlap construction identified borrowing-to-pay-dividends; this is the untested equity counterpart, which carries a different economic interpretation (market timing and overvaluation rather than leverage strain), so evaluating it discriminates between the two stories rather than recombining tested triples. The overlap operator keeps the leg at zero for firms that only issue or only distribute, and using the clean-surplus equity issuance rather than sstk preserves the high-coverage balance-sheet construction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( min( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ), coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: PreRaiseAccrualBuildup
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings management is forward-looking: managers inflate working-capital accruals in the fiscal year *before* they approach the capital markets so that the reported track record supporting the raise looks strong, which means the diagnostic combination is prior-year bloat followed by current-year financing.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal aligns the accrual and financing legs contemporaneously, so none can distinguish accruals that *precede* a raise (window dressing, followed by reversal after the money is in) from accruals that merely accompany it (mechanical growth financing). Lagging only the accrual leg tests that sequencing directly, and because the reversal of a t−1 accrual is still ahead of the t+1 return window, the mispricing should be at least as strong as in the contemporaneous specification while using the same high-coverage balance-sheet items.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( lag( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: RevenueRecognitionAccrualsFinanced
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Not all accruals are equally discretionary: receivable and inventory build are the components managers actually control through channel stuffing, lenient credit terms, and production for stock, whereas payables and tax accruals are largely mechanical, so the manipulation-prone components should carry the mispricing when the firm is also funding itself externally.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the contaminated depreciation-rate idea — which the critique correctly identified as asset-growth squared — with a decomposition that isolates the two accrual components with a genuine discretion story, using the cash-flow-statement items reported with their own sign convention (negated so that a receivable/inventory build scores high). It answers a question the archive cannot: whether the accrual leg's power comes from the discretionary operating components or from the netted aggregate, and it carries no mechanical overlap with the financing leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DollarBloatPlusRaisedCapital
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0))))), at), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The dollar sum of working-capital bloat and newly raised outside capital measures, in commensurate units, how much of the balance sheet is supported by neither operating cash nor retained earnings, and the size of that amount — not merely a firm's cross-sectional rank — determines the severity of the subsequent correction.
input_signals.reasoning: The previous version was algebraically defective because the ib terms cancelled, leaving no accrual content and double-counting dividends; replacing the ib−oancf accrual with the balance-sheet working-capital accrual removes both problems, since dvc now appears only once inside the clean-surplus term and no variable cancels. It is the magnitude-preserving counterpart of CleanSurplusFundedWCBloat (fmb −3.77, alpha −2.2%, coverage 0.110), so it isolates one clean design question — dollars versus ranks — on the archive's best-covered leg pair.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ) ), at ), 1 )

input_signals.name: FullRoundTripDistributions
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(MIN(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), ADD(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(prstkc, 0))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The complete round trip — total outside capital taken in, overlapped against total cash handed out through both dividends and repurchases — measures how much of a firm's shareholder distribution is literally recycled financing, and that recycling is a negative signal exactly when reported profits are accrual-based rather than cash-backed.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested the debt-to-dividend overlap (alpha −1.8%) and the equity-to-dividend overlap (Sharpe −0.50, fmb −3.63) separately, but a firm can fund distributions with whichever source is cheapest, so restricting the overlap to one financing form or one payout form mismeasures the round trip and dilutes both legs. Aggregating both sides before taking the MIN should produce the sharpest version of the mechanism that generated the archive's largest alphas, while the overlap operator keeps investment-driven borrowers and self-funded payers at neutral.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( min( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), add( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), coalesce( prstkc, 0 ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ChronicCapitalRecycling
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(MIN(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), ADD(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(prstkc, 0))), 3), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A single year of funding distributions with fresh capital can be timing or transition, but a firm that recycles outside money into shareholder payouts year after year has a structural inability to fund its own distribution policy, and that chronic state is what makes accrual-based earnings genuinely unreliable.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not an operator swap on the round-trip proposal but a change in the economic object — chronic versus episodic recycling — motivated by the fact that annual overlap flows are lumpy (a single large raise or a one-off special dividend dominates), which is a plausible reason the debt-only overlap achieved only t = −1.44 despite a sound construction. Cumulating three years of the overlap before scaling smooths that lumpiness while keeping the MIN's one-sided interpretation, so both the cross-sectional slope and portfolio stability should improve relative to the one-year version.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( ts_sum( min( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), add( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), coalesce( prstkc, 0 ) ) ), 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternallyMatchedBloatDollars
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0))))), at), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically relevant quantity is the number of dollars of working-capital build that were actually matched by newly raised outside capital — bloat financed from operating cash is self-limiting, and capital raised for genuine investment is not accrual-driven, so only the overlap of the two represents externally financed soft assets.
input_signals.reasoning: The rejected version multiplied a signed magnitude by a positive rank, which perversely made rigid-dividend self-funded firms the strongest buys; taking the MIN of the two dollar flows instead makes the construction one-sided by design — it is large and positive only when bloat and financing are jointly large, and it is negative only for firms that are simultaneously liquidating working capital and returning capital, which is exactly the intended long leg. It preserves dollar magnitude, which produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slope (fmb −4.01), while adding the overlap conditioning that produced the archive's largest alphas, and it uses only balance-sheet items so coverage stays at the archive maximum of about 0.110.

input_signals.name: PayoutAgainstLiquidityFunded
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at))), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(dvc, 0), ADD(che, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A dividend is a strain not when it is large relative to reported earnings — which are themselves suspect — but when it is large relative to the cash the firm actually holds; such a payout can only be sustained by continued access to capital markets, and accrual-heavy earnings make that access fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's payout-strain conditioner measured the dividend against |ib|, an accrual-contaminated denominator that partly re-expresses the accrual leg; measuring it against cash holdings instead makes the conditioner a pure liquidity-commitment ratio and connects the two mechanisms that generated the largest alphas (payout rigidity and absent financial slack). Both are bounded in [0,1] and the comparison against PayoutStrainExternallyFunded isolates whether earnings coverage or liquidity coverage is the operative form of distribution strain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), add( che, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternallyBuiltAssetBaseAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), 5), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Five years of cumulative outside capital measures what fraction of the current asset base was built with investors' money rather than retained cash; firms whose balance sheets are structurally externally financed have no demonstrated ability to self-fund, so accrual-heavy earnings today are far more likely to be an accommodation to that dependence than a temporary timing difference.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the identity-collapsing net-operating-asset construction with a conditioner that is genuinely independent of the accrual leg — a five-year accumulated financing stock rather than a contemporaneous balance-sheet difference — and it directly addresses the generation's central question by converting a flow into a persistent state without importing a leverage characteristic. Unlike the gen-0 cumulative test, the accrual leg is the current-year measure (so the interaction is "structural dependence times current aggressiveness") and the financing stock is built from balance-sheet clean surplus rather than sparse cash-flow items, preserving coverage near 0.09 despite the five-year window.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), 5 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: SoftShareOfGrowthEquityFunded
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), ADD(ABS(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)))), ABS(DELTA(at, 1))))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Two firms can grow their balance sheets identically while one adds plant and the other adds receivables and inventory; what predicts poor returns is the *share* of growth that is soft, and that share is most suspect when the growth was funded by selling equity rather than by retained cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The flow family's alphas are plausibly absorbed by CMA because their accrual and financing legs both scale with total asset growth; expressing the accrual leg as a bounded share of total balance-sheet growth removes the size-of-growth component and leaves only its composition, which the investment factor does not span. Pairing it with clean-surplus net equity issuance keeps the overvaluation-timing interpretation while using high-coverage balance-sheet items.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), add( abs( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ) ), abs( delta( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: RigidityAmplifiedAccrualMagnitude
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Claim rigidity does not create mispricing, it amplifies it symmetrically: among firms with mostly contractual obligations, aggressive accruals are punished harder and genuinely cash-backed earnings are rewarded more, because these are the firms for which the difference between paper profit and cash actually determines solvency.
input_signals.reasoning: Every rigid-claim signal in the archive compresses accruals into a rank, discarding magnitude, which is precisely what the strongest cross-sectional slopes (DollarBloat fmb −4.01, SoftFundingIntensity −3.61) retain — so this tests whether keeping signed accrual magnitude while letting rigidity scale it can deliver the FMB slope that the rank-product family loses. Unlike the gen-4 proposal rejected for symmetric amplification, the hypothesis here is explicitly two-sided and matches the constrained-firm amplification story, so the functional form and the economics agree.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: DividendRaisedOnBorrowedMoney
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(MIN(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), DELTA(COALESCE(dvc, 0), 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Increasing the dividend is a public commitment to future cash payments; doing so in the same year the firm takes in net outside capital means the commitment is being escalated on borrowed strength, and if the earnings behind it are accrual-based the escalation is a signalling gamble rather than a statement of capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the problematic cushion denominator — which could be near zero or negative for exactly the distressed firms it targeted — in favour of an overlap of two flows, the construction with the best design record in this archive, so no division by a possibly-negative capacity is involved. It is also a different economic event from anything tested: the archive's payout legs are all levels or floors, whereas this isolates the *act of raising* the dividend while simultaneously raising capital.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( min( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), delta( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: BoundedAccrualShareFinanced
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(ABS(ib), ABS(oancf)))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is the fraction of reported profit that is not backed by cash, not its size relative to assets: a firm whose entire earnings figure is accrual while its cash flow is negative is qualitatively different from an asset-heavy firm with the same accrual-to-assets ratio, and that qualitative difference is what external funding exposes.
input_signals.reasoning: Every accrual leg in this archive is deflated by assets, which makes it mechanically correlated with asset intensity and heavily outlier-driven; a bounded accrual-share-of-earnings measure in [−1, 1] is a different economic construct — earnings composition rather than balance-sheet intensity — and its boundedness should produce more monotone cross-sectional behaviour without the winsorization crutch. Paired with the standard clean-surplus financing leg it tests the encoding directly against CleanSurplusFundedWCBloat and BookTaxGapFinancedGrowth.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), add( abs( ib ), abs( oancf ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DividendsAbsorbingOperatingCash
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(dvc, 0), ADD(ABS(oancf), COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, COALESCE(dvc, 0)))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically correct test of distribution sustainability is what share of the cash the business actually generates is consumed by the dividend; a firm handing most of its operating cash to shareholders while simultaneously taking capital in from them is running a distribution policy that operations do not support.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested payout strain against reported earnings (|ib|) and against cash holdings (che), and both produced the run's best joint evidence, but never against operating cash flow — the one denominator that directly measures the firm's ability to fund the payout, and the one that makes the strain leg itself an accruals-theme construct rather than a balance-sheet characteristic. This is a two-leg product rather than the rejected triple, so the cross-sectional slope is not diluted by a third rank multiplication.

input_signals.name: SeniorClaimsAheadOfAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dvt, COALESCE(dvc, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Preferred dividends are a claim that ranks ahead of common shareholders and must be served before any residual value accrues to them; when the earnings supporting that seniority structure are accrual-based rather than cash, the common equity is the tranche that absorbs the shortfall.
input_signals.reasoning: Claim *seniority* is the one financing dimension this archive has never touched — every conditioner so far has measured quantity, maturity, composition or rigidity of claims, but none their priority — and the total-minus-common dividend difference isolates it using a reported item (dvt) that no prior signal has used. Firms without preferred stock sit at zero and stay in the neutral middle of the sort, so the extreme bucket contains only genuinely subordinated common equity with weak earnings quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dvt, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: TradeCreditWithdrawalReplacedByMarkets

input_signals.hypothesis: Suppliers monitor their customers more closely than public investors do; when operating liabilities shrink while the firm simultaneously raises capital from markets, informed trade creditors are withdrawing and being replaced by uninformed outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: This inverts a genuine and surprising archive finding: DualSidedWorkingCapitalStrain flipped to a positive alpha (+1.3%) because its payables-build leg predicted *higher* returns, which implies the reverse — payables contraction — is the informative bad state, a reading no signal has yet exploited. Pairing supplier-credit withdrawal with market-capital inflow gives a two-sided informed-versus-uninformed-financier story that is distinct from every quantity, maturity or payout leg tested, and it uses only high-coverage balance-sheet items.

input_signals.hypothesis: The informative event is the year in which the dividend's claim on operating cash jumps — because cash flow fell, the payout rose, or both — and the firm meets the resulting gap by raising outside capital rather than by cutting the distribution.
input_signals.reasoning: The level version of this coverage ratio produced the archive's best slope but only a −2.5% alpha at t −1.89, the signature of a variable that identifies firm type as much as change in condition; differencing it isolates the deterioration event, the same modification that lifted the cash-call conditioner from a null slope to a reliable −3.3% alpha at t −3.69 in gen 8.
